comparison: Both evaluate the in vivo electrophysiological recordings of GGN hyperpolarization (C56-C60, C75). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on adequate sample size and novel observations. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging these as novel functional properties with no challenges to validity.

Both evaluate the dynamic range predictions from computational modeling (C52-C55). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting it remains a model prediction not directly tested in locust. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with reviewers unconvinced due to lack of experimental validation, questioning model design, and requesting claims be presented as predictions rather than definitive statements.

Both evaluate the biophysical modeling of signal propagation (C3, C39-C47, C89, C96). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on detailed modeling with realistic parameters. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 questioning whether this capacity was already demonstrated by Papadopoulou et al., 2011, and requesting better contextualization of novelty.

Both evaluate the morphological characterization of GGN (C25-C33). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on converging evidence from confocal imaging, 3D reconstruction, and quantitative measurements. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 calling the anatomical characterization 'a useful resource' and no challenges to the observations.

Both evaluate the prediction of an unknown olfactory pathway (C5, C77-C81). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting strong timing analysis and nerve-cutting evidence, though the pathway identity remains unknown. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting contradictions in rationale and Reviewer 3 challenging whether PNs/KCs were truly silenced (maxillary palps not addressed).

Both evaluate findings about KC spike rates and high-firing KCs (C68-C70, C98). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on extensive in vivo recordings and model-experiment agreement. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED but notes findings are consistent with Perez-Orive et al., 2002, and requests better contextualization with prior literature.

Both evaluate the model-based findings about high-firing KCs as emergent properties (C71-C74). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on systematic KC removal analysis. Peer review also rates as SUPPORTED, with no fundamental challenges, though Reviewer 3 suggests strengthening the functional interpretation.

Both evaluate model requirements for heterogeneous connectivity and structured input (C65-C66). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on systematic model comparisons. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting quantitative comparison between model and experimental KC distributions, testing different patterns of KC input, and ruling out synchronization effects from timing variability.

Both evaluate the IG-GGN reciprocal connectivity model (C82-C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as part of the broader prediction of an unknown pathway. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting more intuition for the model design and noting that the broad range of IG properties tested is not shown, preventing reader evaluation.
